---    
layout: post    
title: The Curse of Jet-Lag    
image: /assets/images/jetlag.jpg   
---

So, you've just spent hours on a plane, barely got any sleep. Barely keeping yourself awake you make it from the airport to your new home, hotel, hostel ?whatever. You've now finally ready to enter the dreamscape. It takes some time, but you fall asleep

---only to wake up three hours later. You already know that it's over.

It hits you hard and lingers for the rest of the day---well, the rest of the night, actually. Jet lag. 

It doesn't let go, gripping you tightly and constantly reminding you, 

"You're still new here. You don't get the privilege of a good night's sleep. Your body, your mental well-being, it's in my control."

So, you lay in bed, stressing over how much sleep you've been missing. You live in limbo, unable to be awake and unable to be asleep, staring at the ceiling, helpless. You're exhausted but wide awake, trapped in this cycle, wondering when it will finally let you rest. 

At some point, as you lay there, fighting for some sense of normalcy, you debate whether to sleep or get up. Regardless, you can't be productive in this state, and you can't sleep. Stuck in this cycle, until it releases its hold on you. Days? Weeks? Who knows. Only it.
